title.narrative: Provision of food security and livelihoods support for IDP and host community in Nassir County

description.narrative:
The main driver of displacement of civilian populations to and within Nasir County was the continued conflict in South Sudan, which broke out in December 2013, and quickly spread to the Greater Upper Nile region and elsewhere in the country. Nasir County was one of the stronghold of SPLA/IO during the conflict and was the scene of confrontation between the rival forces with people being displaced. The takeover of Nasir town by the SPLA, reportedly led to the complete desertion of the town and surrounding payams by all civilians that were staying there. The general pattern of displacement in Nasir County had been wide dispersement of people into rural areas, and mixing of the IDPs with host communities, with a reported 20,000 people having crossed the border into Ethiopia. Already a stressed and food insecure part of South Sudan, the conflict and resulting displacement within Nasir County had disrupted the seasonal planting and harvest, as well as traditional trade routes, leading to further increase in food insecurity and vulnerability both among IDPs and the host community. The entire Sobat Basin is furthermore very flood-prone during the rainy season, which is beginning, compounding vulnerabilities.
With changes in the conflict dynamics people are beginning to return to Nasir town. Humanitarian assistance may furthermore be required within Nasir town itself, due to the severe disruption of livelihoods that the conflict had already caused, and also taking into consideration the potential damage done to the town during the capture.
Food Security and Livelihoods needs in the area according to assessment conducted by Inter-Agency Rapid Needs Assessment (IRNA) identified the following: General Food Distribution for IDPs and targeted distributions for the host community; Distribution of fishing equipment to further diversify dietary intake and promote self-reliance; Livestock experts should also plan a visit to follow-up and investigate on a sudden increase in diseases
CADA (Community Agribusiness Development Agency), a national NGO which was operating in Nasir throughout the conflict is planning to intervene and provide support to IDPs and Host community to enable them rebuild their lives and re-integrate/integrate to the community. CADA, through this project will provide agriculture inputs (seeds, tools) and trainings as well as fishing gears.
